implementation_statement: Group POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) applies to the BAACS. The OT access standard (NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 based) adds rules for site supervisors, field controllers, and integrator access.

Workforce and RBOC accounts come from SYS-G1 identity governance, driven by HR events. Access control platform administrators and BAS supervisor users sign in through SYS-G1. Gap: about 650 BTI technician accounts are created in the Construction directory and synchronized, but are not tied to assignment end dates, and site supervisors at 47 sites still have local shared accounts.
evidence: Identity governance export; site account survey

implementation_statement: Provisioning, disabling, and quarterly certification campaigns are automated in SYS-G1 identity governance.
Workforce accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled automatically.
Account creation, change, and removal events in SYS-G1 are sent to the group SIEM.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: The SOC alerts on atypical use of BAACS administrator accounts in the central supervisor and the access control platform (for example, off-hours bulk badge exports). Gap: no monitoring of local accounts on site supervisors.

The central BAS supervisor and the access control platform enforce role-based access: RBOC operator, chief engineer (own region only), security operations (own properties only), BTI technician (assigned sites only), and administrator.
evidence: Role catalog; access control platform role export

implementation_statement: Traffic between the OT zones and the corporate network passes through site firewalls with deny-by-default rules where the OT standard is in place. Gap: complete at 61 of 142 owned properties and 19 of 88 hotels only; at the rest OT devices share building IT networks (scenario gap 1).
BAACS platform administration, access control administration (security operations), and approval of integrator access are held by different roles. BTI technicians cannot approve their own sessions.
Users receive least-privilege roles by region and property. Gap: 9 RBOC accounts and 31 BTI accounts hold enterprise-wide administrator rights to the access control platform.
Administrators use separate privileged accounts for administrative work.
Privileged access to the central supervisor and the platform tenant is granted just in time through PAM with approval and session recording.
PAM logs privileged functions and forwards them to the SIEM.
SYS-G1 locks accounts after 10 failed attempts. Site supervisors that support it lock local accounts after 5 failures; older supervisors cannot (documented exception).
Central supervisor, site supervisor, and platform sign-in screens show the group use notice.
Managed workstations, including RBOC consoles and security console PCs, lock after 10 minutes idle; RBOC wall displays are view-only accounts.
Central supervisor and platform sessions end after 30 minutes idle.

Integrator and vendor remote access is supposed to use the BTI remote access gateway: named accounts, MFA, per-session approval by the RBOC, and recording. Gap: always-on vendor remote-support tools with shared accounts remain on site supervisors at 47 sites (scenario gap 1; POAM-006).
evidence: Remote access gateway logs; site tool survey

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Gateway sessions are monitored by the SOC. Gap: sessions through the legacy tools are not visible.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions and site-to-hub links use encrypted tunnels (TLS 1.2 or later; IPsec on the WAN).
Remote access to OT is meant to pass only through the gateway in the provider A hub. Gap: the legacy tools connect out to their vendors' relay services, bypassing the gateway.
No wireless access to OT zones. Building Wi-Fi is segmented from OT where segmentation is complete; rogue wireless scans run quarterly at segmented sites.
RBOC and engineering laptops and tablets are managed devices; unmanaged devices cannot connect to OT zones at segmented sites.

responsible_role: Construction division security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: BTI technicians use group-managed laptops for group sites. Gap: BTI tools (SYS-D5) run in a Construction cloud account outside the group landing zone, under the Construction standard (scenario gap 4; POAM-018).
Group POL-05 and the training standard apply.
Annual security awareness and quarterly phishing exercises for all workforce users, including RBOC staff and BTI technicians.
Role-based OT security training exists for RBOC operators. Gap: chief engineers and hotel engineers have no OT security or manual-operation training at about half the sites.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Logged events are defined in the logging standard: sign-ins, administrator changes, setpoint and schedule changes, badge changes, remote sessions. Gap: site supervisors and door controllers are not configured to send these events.
Central supervisor and platform audit records include user, time, object (point, door, badge), old and new value, and source address.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews central supervisor and access control platform logs daily through SIEM rules. Gap: site-level OT logs are not collected, so site events cannot be reviewed (scenario gap 2; POAM-011).
Central components use provider time services; site supervisors synchronize to the hub time source at segmented sites.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Logs collected centrally are stored in the write-once central log archive, separate from operator accounts.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Collected logs are kept 1 year searchable and 7 years archived.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Audit generation is on for the central supervisor and the platform tenant. Gap: 212 site supervisors at unsegmented or older sites generate only local logs that roll over in days (POAM-011).
Group internal audit assesses common controls once and samples BAACS and division controls each year (P07).

Interconnections with SYS-D5 (BTI tools), SYS-D2 (visitor management), SYS-D6 (hotel PMS for back-of-house badges), and the BAS optimization service are documented. Gap: no written interconnection terms with SYS-D5 or the optimization service.
BAACS weaknesses are tracked in the group POA&M (P07).
Monthly BAACS metrics to the Group CISO: segmentation progress, legacy remote tools removed, inventory coverage, patch status.
Annual penetration test of the central supervisor and platform tenant. Gap: site-level OT has not been penetration tested; a test at 3 pilot sites is planned for 2027 Q1.
Baseline configurations exist for the central supervisor, new site supervisors, and door controllers. Gap: network diagrams for 74 legacy sites are missing or out of date.
Changes to central components and to site programs go through the OT change process (RBOC approval, BTI implementation, rollback plan). Emergency changes are reviewed the next business day.
Setpoint logic and schedule changes are tested on a staging supervisor before release to many sites.
Only the RBOC change role and named BTI engineers can deploy programs to site supervisors through the central supervisor.

Cloud components follow landing-zone guardrails. Site supervisors follow the OT hardening baseline where segmented. Gap: 14 field controller models at older sites still had manufacturer default passwords in the P07 sample.

Unneeded services are disabled on new site supervisors. Gap: P07 found BACnet/IP and web management reachable from building IT networks at unsegmented sites and 3 video recorders reachable from the internet (POAM-012).

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: The OT asset inventory combines BTI device lists, passive sensor discovery, and platform exports. Gap: about 74% complete; passive discovery runs at 38 sites only (scenario gap 2; POAM-008).
Software licenses for BAS and platform software are tracked by group procurement.
Users cannot install software on RBOC consoles or engineering workstations; BTI laptops are managed by the Construction division.

The BAACS contingency plan covers loss of the central supervisor and the access control platform. Gap: manual operating procedures for HVAC and doors exist at only some properties and hotels (scenario gap 3; POAM-015).
evidence: BAACS contingency plan; site procedure tracker

implementation_statement: The central supervisor restore from backup was tested once (2025). Gap: no multi-site restore exercise, and no restore test of site programs from the group vault.
Backups are stored in the immutable vault in provider B, in a separate account and identity domain.
Planned: a standby central supervisor in provider B (2027 Q2). Today the supervisor is rebuilt from backup.

The central supervisor, historian, and platform configuration are backed up daily to the immutable vault. Gap: site supervisor configurations and field controller programs for about 40% of sites exist only in the BTI repository (scenario gap 3; POAM-009).
evidence: Backup job report; site program coverage report

implementation_statement: Recovery procedures exist for the central supervisor. Gap: no procedure or tested capacity to reload many site supervisors at once (POAM-009).
RBOC, security operations, and administrators authenticate through SYS-G1. Gap: shared local accounts on site supervisors at 47 sites and on older field controllers.
Phishing-resistant MFA for all privileged access to the central supervisor and platform tenant.
MFA (number matching) for all non-privileged workforce access to BAACS consoles.

New site supervisors and door controllers authenticate to the central services with device certificates. Gap: older field controllers on BACnet/IP cannot authenticate (compensated by segmentation where complete).
Identifiers are unique and never reused; badge credential numbers are unique per badge holder.

Workforce authenticators are managed in SYS-G1. Device and local OT passwords are to be stored in the group vault. Gap: local OT credentials for about 40% of sites are held in the BTI credential vault (SYS-D5), not the group vault (POAM-002).
Tenant administrators who manage their own employees' badges in the access control platform authenticate through the platform with MFA.
Incident response training for SOC and RBOC staff each year.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Group incident handling applies to the BAACS. Gap: OT-specific playbooks (contain a site without losing control of plant) exist for ransomware only, and the BTI unit has no defined role in group incident response (POAM-005).

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Incidents are tracked in the SOC case system.
Group POL-03 and the P08 matrix set reporting. Gap: the cross-division notification matrix has not been exercised (scenario gap 7; POAM-004).
Group incident response plan with the P08 runbook. Gap: the BAACS runbook has not been tested in a cross-division exercise.
Maintenance on BAACS components is scheduled through work orders in SYS-D1 and change records.
Nonlocal maintenance should use the BTI gateway with MFA and recording. Gap: the legacy tools at 47 sites (same finding as AC-17).
Maintenance personnel are BTI employees or approved manufacturer technicians, listed by site.
Media from decommissioned supervisors, NVRs, and workstations is wiped or destroyed with a certificate.
USB media is blocked on RBOC consoles. Gap: engineering workstations at about half the sites still allow USB storage for program loading.

responsible_role: Commercial Property director of security operations
implementation_statement: Access to engineering rooms, BAS panels, and head-end equipment is limited to authorized engineers and BTI technicians by badge role.

responsible_role: Commercial Property director of security operations
implementation_statement: Engineering rooms and head-end closets are badge-controlled and on camera.

responsible_role: Commercial Property director of security operations
implementation_statement: Door forced and held alarms are monitored by the security console and the RBOC.
This SSP.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) acknowledged by all users, including BTI technicians and tenant administrators.
The OT security architecture (zones and conduits per NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3) is defined in the OT standard.
Group information security program plan (POL-01).
The Group CISO leads the program; the Group OT security lead owns the OT program.
Group risk management strategy with tolerance and acceptance authority (P01).
Background screening for RBOC, security operations, and BTI staff before access is granted.
Termination events disable SYS-G1 accounts within 4 hours and revoke badges through the access control platform.

responsible_role: Commercial Property director of security operations
implementation_statement: Guard contractor and parking operator staff are covered by contract terms. Gap: guard contractor remote video viewers use a shared login (POAM-016).

control_name: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information
implementation_statement: Purposes for badge, video, and visitor data are documented. Gap: no documented purpose and consent basis for face templates in the verification pilot (P10).
Badge and video data may be used for building security only. Gap: vendor terms allow use of customer video to improve vendor models; no opt-out exercised (P10).
The BAACS is categorized High (section 6 of this plan).
Group and division risk assessments cover the BAACS (P01 GR-01 to GR-03).

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Central components are scanned weekly. OT devices are assessed by passive discovery and vendor advisories. Gap: 212 site supervisors run older software and 58 run an operating system past vendor support (POAM-010).
Critical components (central supervisor, gateway, site supervisors at critical-occupancy sites) are identified. Gap: criticality analysis not done for hotels.
Group contracts include the security addendum. Gap: the 2021 intercompany services agreement with the BTI unit has no security terms (POAM-018).

External services (access control platform, BAS optimization service, video analytics) are reviewed under POL-01. Gap: the BAS optimization service and the analytics features were enabled without review.
Unsupported components are recorded with compensating controls. Gap: 58 site supervisors run an operating system past vendor support; replacement plan through 2027.
Provider DDoS protection on the central supervisor and gateway endpoints.

The hub and site firewalls enforce the OT zone model where deployed. Gap: segmentation complete at 80 of 230 owned and hotel sites, and managed buildings are segmented only where owners funded it (POAM-007).

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default, allow by exception at segmented sites. Gap: not at unsegmented sites.
Site-to-hub traffic travels in encrypted tunnels; platform traffic uses TLS.
Cryptographic protection in transit as for SC-8.
Remote sessions through the gateway end after 30 minutes idle and at the approved window end.
Keys for central components are customer-managed in provider key management.

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SaaS)
implementation_statement: Badge holder data, face templates, and video exports are encrypted at rest by the platform vendor; central supervisor disks are encrypted with group-managed keys.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; disk encryption settings

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Central components are patched monthly. Site supervisors are updated by BTI during scheduled visits. Gap: no patch time standard for OT; median age of site supervisor software is 26 months.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: EDR on the central supervisor, RBOC consoles, and engineering workstations that support it; application allow-listing on site supervisors that cannot run EDR (segmented sites only).

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: The SOC monitors central components. Passive OT monitoring sensors cover 38 sites. Gap: no OT monitoring at the other 226 sites (scenario gap 2; POAM-003).

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: Inbound and outbound traffic at segmented sites is monitored. Gap: legacy remote tools' outbound connections were not alerting.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G2 Group SOC, SIEM, and EDR
implementation_statement: The SOC tracks CISA ICS advisories and manufacturer bulletins for BAACS products and opens tickets.
Program changes are compared with the BTI repository version before deployment. Gap: no integrity check of programs running on site supervisors.
Video is kept 30 days on recorders; badge transaction history 2 years. Gap: tailgating alert clips are kept 1 year by default, and the face template retention rule is not set.
Supply chain controls cover BAACS products and integrators. Gap: the BTI unit is treated as an internal team, not as a supplier.
BAACS products are bought only from the group approved-products list, which excludes covered telecommunications and video surveillance equipment under Section 889 group-wide.
Supplier assessments use SOC 2 reports for SaaS vendors. Gap: the BAS optimization service provider has not been assessed.
Components are bought from manufacturers or authorized distributors only.
